prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence is still thin for adoption (new_screen, redesign), home (new_flow), and choose_path (reorder) changes because each has only 1 test or non-conclusive/conflicting results.
Evidence is still thin for finish (new_screen) changes because the two completed tests disagreed after noise correction (+9.3% vs -7.1%).
Reordering sign_in steps was helpful overall, backed by 3 winning tests (+8.8%, +4.2%, and +4.7%), though no clear effect was seen in the other 3 tests.
Predictions were generally too high across most tests, but were too low for the round 2 finish test and round 8 sign_in reorder test.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, new_screen: -2.3% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- adoption, redesign: -3.7% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- choose_path, reorder: -2.7% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_screen: +0.1% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- home, new_flow: -10.2% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: +3.4% after noise correction, 6 test(s)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 87.7%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 77.0%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 25.5%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [adoption, new_screen] Companion Emotion Preview Stage Screen: Insert a new screen before adoption certificate showing how the pet reacts with different emotions. (why: 39.1% of users drop during adoption, and support tickets report post-onboarding confusion on how to interact with pets.)
1: [home, new_flow] Pet Generation Stage Layout Flow: Rebuild the waiting screen into a structured stage layout with step-by-step rendering status. (why: The waiting screen has a high median wait time of 201s (mean 2336s), leading to user drop-off during background generation.)
2: [finish, redesign] Home Intro Card Layout Redesign: Redesign the home intro finish screen into a structured card layout presenting desktop control instructions. (why: Finish step takes a median of 395s and multiple support emails cite confusion about hiding, controlling, or talking to pets.)
3: [sign_in, hint] Account Sync Security Sign-In Hint: Add a prominent hint to the sign-in screen assuring users that pet progress syncs safely to their account. (why: 8 support messages (the largest email theme) reported pets missing or reset after signing in again.)
4: [home, wait_info] Waiting Engine Background Processing Notification: Enable background desktop notifications and time estimation on the waiting screen. (why: Long wait times on the home step (median 201s, mean 2336s) cause users to abandon onboarding while pet assets build.)
5: [adoption, incentive] Pick Friend Favorite Companion Choice Badge: Add a recommendation badge component to highlight popular choices on the pick_friend screen. (why: Adoption conversion is low (60.9%), indicating decision fatigue when picking or generating pets.)
6: [finish, notification] Home Intro Quick Control Guide Text: Add a visual highlight text block on the home_intro screen explaining basic pet commands. (why: Multiple support emails describe confusion over how to control, hide, or talk to the pet once setup finishes.)

scores.note: Target step has highest drop (39.1%) and support mail context, but new screens in adoption previously performed poorly (-2.3%).
Home step drop is notable, but previous new_flow attempt failed significantly (-10.2% relative lift).
Strong evidence from support and time metrics, but full redesigns carry execution risk and high engineering cost.
Step conversion is already high (87.7%), but sign_in changes consistently perform well and cost is low.
Addresses 201s median wait time without risking a full flow rebuild.

Directly addresses widespread user confusion reported in support emails via low-cost text highlight.
